mainTopic: Does wrong intent at שחיטה alone create full פיגול? Challenges from עולא, אילפא and the תודה loaves, and a suggested proof for רב גידל from a ברייתא about מעילה.
overview: This amud continues a discussion of רב גידל's view: wrong intent during שחיטה alone does not create full פיגול. The גמרא first challenges this from עולא's קל וחומר about the קמיצה, and answers that עולא meant only an איסורא leading toward פיגול. Next, רבינא challenges רב אשי from אילפא, whose case of two סימנים cut with different wrong intentions seems to show that שחיטה alone makes פיגול. רב אשי answers that the final status is decided only once the blood is sprinkled. The גמרא then asks why the תודה loaves become holy at the שחיטה, and explains that 'קדש' there only means they can become פסול and need שריפה. Finally, the גמרא tries to support רב גידל from a ברייתא: 'פיגול is always subject to מעילה.' Two attempts to push off this proof are each challenged as making the ברייתא teach something obvious. First, it might be a case where the blood was not sprinkled. Second, it might be about an עולה. The discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from עולא's own קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that עולא meant only a lesser prohibited status. עולא's own reasoning seems to say the handful becomes real פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But עולא taught: if this act brings other things to פיגול, then the item itself surely becomes פיגול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier answer, which said עולא meant only a 'prohibited state' and not true פיגול. It quotes עולא's own words, which sound like full פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא argued with a קל וחומר: taking the קמיצה with wrong intent makes the rest of the מנחה פיגול, so the handful itself should certainly be פיגול. That sounds like real פיגול coming from a single act with wrong intent. If so, an offering of lesser holiness slaughtered with wrong intent should also become full פיגול from that act alone, without needing wrong intent at the sprinkling.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made invalid by intent to eat it or burn it beyond its proper time. Eating it carries כרת.
'All the more so.' This is the punchline of a קל וחומר.
Reasoning from a weaker case to a stronger one.

phrases.english: But didn't he teach:
phrases.notes: 'He' is עולא, whose statement the earlier answer was explaining away.

phrases.english: If it brings others to פיגול,
phrases.notes: 'Others' means the rest of the מנחה, which the קמיצה makes פיגול.

phrases.english: is it not all the more so for itself!
phrases.notes: 'Itself' is the handful (קמיצה) that was taken with the wrong intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the earlier answer, which read עולא as referring only to a prohibited state.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that עולא's 'פיגול' means only a lesser prohibition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר that ends in 'all the more so it is פיגול' sounds like full פיגול, not a lesser status.

steps.title: Here too it means a prohibition leading toward פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even in the קל וחומר, עולא means only a prohibited state that can lead to פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too means a prohibition that brings it toward פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the earlier answer. Even inside the קל וחומר, עולא did not mean full פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר proves only that the handful gets the same lesser status: an איסורא that is on the way to פיגול. Full פיגול comes only if there is also wrong intent when the handful is offered on the altar. So the earlier reading of עולא still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition, or a prohibited status. Here it is less than full פיגול.
'That brings to.' It leads toward a status but does not complete it.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'brings to פיגול' as 'is already פיגול.' The answer depends on the difference between starting the path to פיגול and completing it.

phrases.english: This too is a prohibition
that brings it to פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא נָמֵי, אִיסּוּרָא דְּמַיְיתֵי לִידֵי פִּיגּוּל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר seemed to prove the handful becomes full פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר gives the handful only the same lesser status, an איסורא leading toward פיגול.

steps.title: רבינא's challenge from אילפא's two-סימנים case
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי from אילפא. אילפא limits the מחלוקת on mixed intentions to two separate parts of the service, and his example assumes שחיטה alone can make an offering פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But אילפא said the מחלוקת is about two parts of the service. For example, someone says, 'I am cutting the first סימן intending beyond its time, and the second סימן intending outside its place.' But within one part of the service, everyone agrees it is a mixture of intentions!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a new challenge from אילפא. אילפא explained where the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and the חכמים about two wrong intentions applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה holds that intent beyond the time followed by intent outside the place makes the offering פיגול. אילפא says this applies only when the two intents come during separate acts, like cutting each סימן in שחיטה. If they come in one act, everyone agrees it is mixed and not פיגול. His example assumes the first סימן, cut with intent beyond its time, already makes פיגול through שחיטה alone. That goes against the view that שחיטה alone is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute. Here it is the dispute of רבי יהודה and the חכמים about two wrong intentions.
One part of the Temple service, such as שחיטה, קבלה, הולכה or זריקה.
One of the two organs cut in שחיטה: the windpipe or the food pipe.
Intent to eat or burn beyond its time, which makes פיגול, or outside its place, which only makes it פסול.
A mixture of intentions, which does not create פיגול.
'Everyone agrees.' Both sides of the dispute accept this point.

steps.whatToRemember: אילפא's case only works if wrong intent during שחיטה alone can make an offering פיגול. That is the problem רבינא is raising.
steps.whyThisMatters: אילפא treats cutting each סימן as its own part of the service. If wrong intent while cutting one סימן were enough to make פיגול, that would go against the view that שחיטה alone does not create פיגול. The next step answers this.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
But didn't Ilfa say:
The dispute is in two parts of the service,
for example, where he said:
'I am slaughtering the first organ beyond its time,
and the second organ outside its place,'
but in one part of the service,
everyone agrees it is a mixture of intentions!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: וְהָאָמַר אִילְפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against the view that wrong intent at שחיטה alone does not create full פיגול.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that wrong intent at שחיטה alone does not make an offering full פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אילפא's case has פיגול created by the first סימן alone, which requires wrong intent at שחיטה to be enough for פיגול.

steps.title: Once the blood is sprinkled, the picture becomes clear
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי agrees with אילפא's case. He explains that once the blood is sprinkled, we see whether the intentions happened in one part of the service or in two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. When he sprinkles the blood, the matter will become clear: whether the intentions were in one service or in two services.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא's challenge from אילפא. He agrees that אילפא's case works, but says the final status is only decided once the blood is sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא argued that אילפא's example assumes שחיטה alone makes פיגול. רב אשי answers that the final status is settled only at זריקה, when the blood is sprinkled. At that point we know whether the mixed intentions were in one עבודה, where there is no מחלוקת, or in two עבודות, where רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, indeed, that is so
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
The matter will be revealed, it becomes clear

phrases.english: Indeed, so it is,
when he sprinkles, the matter will be revealed:
phrases.notes: He means that once the blood is sprinkled with the פיגול intention, we can look back and judge the whole case.

phrases.english: whether it was during one service,
or during two services.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי, לְכִי זָרֵיק תִּיגַּלֵּי מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge from אילפא in step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the final status at a later point: the decision waits until זריקה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אילפא's case seemed to show that שחיטה alone makes an offering פיגול
steps.terutzMaskana: שחיטה alone does not make פיגול. Once the blood is sprinkled, we judge whether the intentions were in one עבודה or in two.

steps.title: Then the תודה loaves should also wait for the sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if everything waits for the sprinkling, then in the case of the תודה the loaves should also not become holy until the blood is sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, regarding the תודה as well, it should only happen once he sprinkles!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's answer using the earlier משנה about a תודה slaughtered with a wrong intention, where the loaves become holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if one slaughters a תודה with an intention beyond its time, the loaves become קדוש right away. If שחיטה alone does not make פיגול, then nothing should happen to the loaves until זריקה. Yet the משנה connects their holiness to the שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanksgiving offering, brought together with loaves
If so, a phrase that introduces a challenge

phrases.english: If so,
regarding the thanks offering as well,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה from the previous daf: if one slaughters a תודה with a wrong intention, the loaves become holy.

phrases.english: it should wait until he sprinkles!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, גַּבֵּי תוֹדָה נָמֵי, עַד דְּזָרֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 4 by applying it to the תודה case
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that status is decided only at זריקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says the loaves become holy at the שחיטה. That suggests the שחיטה alone is enough, so the status should not have to wait for the sprinkling.

steps.title: 'Holy' only means the loaves can become פסול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'קדש' in the תודה משנה does not mean the loaves are fully holy. It only means they are holy enough to become פסול and need burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'became holy' mean? It means holy enough to become disqualified, so that they need to be burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the word 'קדש' in a lighter way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'קדש' meant that the loaves are subject to מעילה, they would need to be fully holy. Here it only means that the loaves are connected enough to the קרבן to become פסול and require שריפה. That lighter status does not require real פיגול at the שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Became holy
To become disqualified
Burning, required for disqualified holy items

steps.confusionAlert: 'קדש' here does not mean the loaves are fully holy, so that one would be liable for מעילה. It only means they are holy enough to become פסול.

phrases.english: What does 'became sanctified' mean?
To be disqualified, so that it requires burning.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the word 'קדש' in the משנה in a lighter way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'קדש' meant the loaves are fully holy, which would need real פיגול at the שחיטה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'קדש' only means the loaves can become פסול and need שריפה, so no פיגול at the שחיטה is needed
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's reading holds: שחיטה alone does not make פיגול. The תודה loaves only reach the lighter status of being able to become פסול.

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems to support רב גידל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a proof for רב גידל from a ברייתא: one is always liable for מעילה with פיגול, even after the blood was sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him: 'With פיגול, one is always liable for מעילה.' Doesn't this mean even though the blood was sprinkled? So it supports him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to back up רב גידל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, sprinkling the blood properly takes the meat out of מעילה. The ברייתא says פיגול is 'always' subject to מעילה. The גמרא reads 'always' as 'even after the blood was sprinkled' with the פיגול intention, which matches רב גידל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him? This introduces a suggested proof.
One is liable for מעילה, misusing holy property
Always

phrases.english: Shall we say that this supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב גידל, whose view is being discussed.

phrases.english: With פיגול, one is always liable for misuse of it.

phrases.aramaic: לָאו אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיזְּרִיק דָּם,
phrases.english: Does it not mean even though the blood was sprinkled,
and so it supports him!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ: הַפִּיגּוּל לְעוֹלָם מוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רב גידל to suggesting outside support for him
steps.raayaObject: רב גידל's ruling about פיגול and מעילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'הפיגול לעולם מועלין בו', read as 'even after the blood was sprinkled'
steps.whyThisMatters: The word 'לעולם' carries the whole proof. Whether it really means 'even after the blood was sprinkled' decides whether the ברייתא supports רב גידל.

steps.title: Maybe the blood was not sprinkled yet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof for רב גידל. It suggests the ברייתא is talking about a case where the blood was not sprinkled yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The ברייתא may be talking about a case where the blood was not sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 7. It says the ברייתא could be talking about an offering whose blood was never sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גידל needs a case where the blood of a פיגול offering was sprinkled and מעילה still applies. If the blood was never sprinkled, the offering is still fully קדשי ה׳, so מעילה applies for a simple reason. Then the ברייתא tells us nothing about רב גידל's point.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח, the step that finishes the main service
Misusing הקדש for personal benefit, which is forbidden

phrases.english: No, it is where he did not sprinkle the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 7 by reading the ברייתא as a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof for רב גידל from the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be talking about an offering whose blood was not sprinkled, so it says nothing about after the sprinkling.

steps.title: Then the ברייתא would be teaching something obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that rejection. If the blood was not sprinkled, the ברייתא would be telling us something everyone already knows.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not sprinkle the blood, why does the ברייתא need to say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rejection from step 8. It asks why a ברייתא would bother to teach something so plain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the sprinkling, an offering of קדשי קדשים is still fully קדשי ה׳ and under מעילה, פיגול or not. So reading the ברייתא as a case before the sprinkling makes it teach nothing new. A ברייתא is assumed to teach something worth saying, so this reading looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: Why say it? Meaning: this is obvious, so there is no need to teach it

phrases.english: If it is where he did not sprinkle the blood,
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: Before the sprinkling, מעילה clearly applies, so this would be obvious.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּלֹא זָרַק הַדָּם, מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 8 by showing it makes the ברייתא pointless.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the ברייתא as a case where the blood was not sprinkled (step 8)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Before the sprinkling, מעילה obviously applies, so the ברייתא would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: The blood was sprinkled, but the case is an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new way to push off the proof. The blood really was sprinkled, but the ברייתא is about an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it really is where he sprinkled the blood. But when that ברייתא was taught, it was about an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first rejection and tries a different one. It agrees the blood was sprinkled, but says the ברייתא is only about an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גידל's point is that sprinkling with פיגול does not take an offering out of מעילה. But an עולה stays under מעילה even after a proper sprinkling, because no person ever gets to eat it. So the ברייתא could be about an עולה and still not prove רב גידל's rule for other offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the last idea and offers a new one
Really; in truth (the case is like this)
Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the ברייתא is wrong. It is only saying the ברייתא might be limited to an עולה, so it cannot prove רב גידל's rule for other offerings.

phrases.english: Rather: it really is where he sprinkled,
and when that ברייתא was taught,
it was about an עולה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לְעוֹלָם דְּזָרֵיק, וְכִי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא, בְּעוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives up the reading from step 8 after the challenge in step 9, and offers a new reason the proof fails.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof for רב גידל from the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be only about an עולה, which stays under מעילה even after sprinkling for its own reason.

steps.title: An עולה would also be obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second rejection too. If the ברייתא is about an עולה, it is obvious, because the whole עולה belongs to גבוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is about an עולה, that is obvious, since all of it belongs to the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rejection from step 10 the same way it attacked step 8. An עולה being under מעילה is plain and does not need a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is burned completely on the מזבח, and no כהן or owner ever eats it. So it never leaves the status of קדשי ה׳, even after the sprinkling, and מעילה clearly applies. Reading the ברייתא as about an עולה again makes it teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
The Most High; belonging to הקדש and the מזבח, not to people

steps.whyThisMatters: Both ways of pushing off the proof have now run into the same challenge, that the ברייתא would be teaching something obvious. This makes the proof for רב גידל look stronger.

phrases.english: If it is about an עולה, it is obvious,
since all of it belongs to the Most High.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בְּעוֹלָה, פְּשִׁיטָא, דְּגָבוֹהַּ הִיא כּוּלַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 10 by showing it also makes the ברייתא pointless.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the ברייתא as only about an עולה (step 10)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עולה belongs entirely to גבוה, so it is obviously under מעילה even after sprinkling. The ברייתא would be teaching nothing new.
